_README: Cross-tree quirk registry. hal-forks.json records WHERE trees diverge and why;
this records WHICH FIX must be present in WHICH tree, so a fix found in one
generation is not silently missing from another.
Checked by scripts/hal-quirk-check.py (./dev.py hal-quirks, part of ./dev.py gate).
issue      the issue that found it
symptom    what it looks like when absent - the log line or the failure
applies_to trees/files that MUST carry it, each with a marker that proves it
exempt     trees that must NOT carry it, with the reason
marker     a regex that must appear in the file (the fix's fingerprint)
Adding a quirk is part of fixing a bug, not an afterthought: if a quirk could
plausibly affect another tree, it gets an entry even when that tree is exempt.

udma-rx-stream-flush-before-state-change.symptom: [eth rx] warn: dma state didn't change to Normal / error -110; a failed adapter_stop on one port then poisons adapter_init on the next in the same U-Boot session
udma-rx-stream-flush-before-state-change.root_cause: An RX UDMA that can still receive never reaches quiescence: it keeps processing new arrivals while state_set_wait() waits for IDLE, so the wait expires. The stream must be stopped and the FIFOs flushed FIRST.

modules/al_eth/al_hal_eth_main.c.note: gen A (4.1.37). Staged into the U-Boot build by scripts/stage_hal.py (#256), so this one edit covers Linux AND U-Boot.

modules/al_ssm/al_hal_udma_main.c.note: gen B (AL SDK 4.19) - vendor already ships it, behind the flush_stream argument.

exempt.modules/al_hal/al_hal_udma_main.c: Holds al_udma_state_set() only - no wait loop, so no predicate to fix. al_dma calls the bare setter and never waits, so it cannot hit this timeout. If al_dma ever gains a wait, it inherits this quirk - see #342.
exempt.tx/m2s side: M2S has no FLUSH/STOP_PREFETCH bits and no inbound traffic to drop. A TX engine that will not quiesce has a descriptor stuck in flight, which is #253, not a missing flush.

udma-queue-reset-before-reuse.symptom: A module reload meets queues the hardware still thinks are running: alloc_chan_resources fails -EIO, or the engine silently does nothing. rmmod/modprobe does NOT reset UDMA hardware state - only a reboot does, which is why this was believed to be a hardware quirk.
udma-queue-reset-before-reuse.root_cause: UDMA queue state lives in hardware and survives the driver. Every module that owns UDMA queues must reset them on bring-up rather than assume a clean engine.

modules/al_dma/al_dma_drv.c.note: Per channel, tx+rx, skipping queues not AL_QUEUE_ENABLED.

modules/al_ssm/al_ssm_main.c.note: Where the fix was first made (#167); al_dma's comment cites it.

exempt.modules/al_nand, al_thermal, al_sgpo, al: Own no UDMA queues - no engine state to carry across a reload.
